title: Chainalysis Breach Exposes All Users' Credentials, Forces Shutdown of Key Services
summary: Blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis has revealed that its ongoing investigation into the agentic cyber attack targeting its systems also exposed names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all users.

title: Hackers Hide Linux Backdoor in Control Web Panel Server to Execute Commands Without Logs
summary: A backdoor has been found hiding in the web server that runs Control Web Panel (CWP), a free panel for managing Linux hosting servers, researchers at QiAnXin's XLab said this week.
card_summary: A backdoor has been found hiding in the web server that runs Control Web Panel (CWP), a free panel for managing Linux hosting servers, researchers at QiAnXin's XLab said this week.

sections.mitigation: Installing it takes root access, so the attackers must already control the server.

email_summary: A backdoor has been found hiding in the web server that runs Control Web Panel (CWP), a free panel for managing Linux hosting servers, researchers at QiAnXin's XLab said this week. The backdoored web server executes commands that attackers send via web requests, and those requests never appear in its access logs.

title: Experts Demonstrate Barracuda Email Security Gateway Chain Enabling Root Access Without Login
summary: Two flaws in Barracuda's Email Security Gateway, an email-filtering appliance, can be chained to run commands on it as root, its highest level of access, with no login required.
card_summary: Two flaws in Barracuda's Email Security Gateway, an email-filtering appliance, can be chained to run commands on it as root, its highest level of access, with no login required.

sections.mitigation: The company released patches on Monday, and the security firm watchTowr detailed the attack chain on Thursday.

email_summary: Two flaws in Barracuda's Email Security Gateway, an email-filtering appliance, can be chained to run commands on it as root, its highest level of access, with no login required. Tracked as CVE-2026-116606.
